*Decisions for decision making*

## Chapter 2: Representation

### Degrees of belief & probability

It is essential to be able to compare the plausibility of different statements
involving problems of uncertainty. The representation that proposition $A$ is
more plausible than proposition $B$, or If $A$ represents "my actuator failed",
and $B$ represents "my sensor failed," would be written as $A \succ B$.
Utilizing the basic relation $\succ$, the following may be defined:

- $A \prec B \text{ iff } B \succ A$
- $A \backsim B \text{ iff neither } A \succ B \text{ nor } B \succ A$
- $A \succeq B \text{ iff } A \succ B \text{ or } A \backsim B$
- $A \preceq B \text{ iff } B \succ A \text{ or } A \backsim B$

We want to make certain assumptions about the relationships induced by the
operators $\succ$, $\backsim$,& $\prec$. The assumptions of *universal
comparability* requires exactly one of the following to hold:
$A \succ B$, $B \backsim A$, or $A \prec B$. The assumption of *transitivity*
requires that if $A \succeq B$ and $B \succeq C$, then $A \succeq C$. These
transivity assumptions lead to an ability to represent plausibility by
real-valued function $P$ that has the following two properties:

$$
\begin{align}
P(A) > P(B) \text{ iff } A \succ B \\
P(A) = P(B) \text{ iff } A \backsim B
\end{align}
$$
